title: My take on a PSO-like
author: gamerqc
selftext:
[https://youtu.be/-E20OJ\_EfxU](https://youtu.be/-E20OJ_EfxU)

Hey all,

I thought I'd share my prototype here. One of my favorite games of all time is **Phantasy Star Online**, and I'm always surprised that we never got a proper 'clone'. In my opinion, PSO2 and New Genesis stray too far from what made the original games (up to Blue Burst) so great: simple dungeons, methodical combat, memorable weapons, etc. 

With the newly improved AI models, I'm finally able to test my ideas in working conditions. For the record, I'm using Claude with Sonnet 5.5 on the basic package (around $30 CAD per month). At some point I tried Opus 5.5 but it drained my tokens too fast. My workflow is probably not ideal since I'm using the browser discussion tool. I plan on having a GIT repository so I can see commits, revert if needed, etc. 

I didn't start with a 'one prompt make no mistakes' philosophy. Rather, I sliced my vision into numerous development passes. I started with basic stuff like the engine (Godot 4.6+), 3D, WASD/arrow for movement, third-person perspective, left click for attacks, space to jump. I had the main HUB created (with no NPCs at first) and a portal to reach the first dungeon (Forest 1). Once this worked, I quickly moved to dungeon procedural generation, which hit quite a few hurdles due to laser gates not closing all the gaps, out of place props, etc. Once I was satisfied with the basic dungeon generation, I added random monster spawns, four monster types with different attack behaviors, basic loot with quite a few different types, points of interest, a detailed minimap, random chests, a dragon boss (three phases), a bunch of unique weapons and more.

Right now there's only one 'family, and class, but I plan on having 3 of each for the prototype. Weapons are currently not restricted for testing purposes, but I'm undergoing a massive game balance overhaul right now that will lock some weapon types to classes (like Diablo). Right now I have laser sabers, laser swords, gauntlets, guns, energy launchers, magical staffs, energy bows, rune swords and maybe I'm forgetting some off the top of my head. 

The prototype has programmatically-generated art assets so there's no real DA on purpose, and few animations. But I did incorporate a lot of feedback based on previous versions, including hit stops, flashes before attacks, better lock-on, improved UI, etc. All in all, I've been working on this project for less than 2 weeks and already made significant progress (IMO). SFX are made by Claude, while the few tracks have been generated by Google Gemini. I actually quite like the HUB song, as well as the combat and boss song of the second area.

To give you an ideas, here's an overview of what I've been able to accomplish so far. It's very impressive that it all works IMO, and really will help further democratize video game development for people like me who know neither how to code nor how to create assets. 

* Title screen
* Save slots
* Basic character creation
* Basic progression (levels and stats)
* Many weapon types with different playstyles (melee, ranged and magic)
* Weapon drops based on loot tables with different rarities, including uniques like a shotgun, a magical broom and a tortoise shell (armor)
* Four monsters for the Forest area, including stronger variants appearing from Forest 2
* Six mutators: monsters can randomly spawn one and add its effect(s), like DETONATING which causes a small AOE explosion that can damage both players and monsters nearby
* First dungeon: Ancient Forest 1-2-3, with a different skybox for each (sunny/dusk/night)
* First boss: Drakion, a dragon (three phases)
* Second dungeon: Infested Colony 1-2, much more industrial with four new types of monsters
* Second boss: Parasite (two phases, with the second taking place in space with floating platforms)
* HUB NPCs to sell/buy items, as well as gamble for better loot (Gheed style)
* Anima Seed to resurrect when incapacitated
* Random chests, one of which triggers monster wave(s) before opening
* Breakable crates
* Locked gates
* Opening/closing airlock doors
* Dodge (SHIFT), also used to move faster through dungeons (will be reoworked though)
* ECHO system: just like MAGs from PSO, these critters follow you around, gain levels and can activate a special skill (Overdrive). I designed them to be much more interesting though: they evolve based on your playstyle. In a future version, I'll add more player agency too as the current implementation lacks complexity on purpose

There's much more to it of course. My point being, don't be afraid to experiment. I keep my scope limited but already have so many intertwined systems, it's kind of impressive. I'd love to show this prototype down the line and maybe get some artists on board to create real assets, while keeping the low poly/Dreamcast esthetic.
